stem: What assurance did this argument give to those who opposed ratifying the Constitution?

options.label: A
options.text: The amendment process would allow state governments to nullify federal law.

options.label: B
options.text: Making the federal government superior to state governments would ensure greater stability.

options.label: C
options.text: The rights of citizens would be better protected by having both federal and state levels of government.

options.label: D
options.text: Giving greater power to the federal government would allow it to assist states in times of crisis.

visual_elements: In the . . . republic of America, the power surrendered by the people is first divided between two distinct governments, and then the portion allotted to each subdivided among distinct and separate departments. Hence a double security arises to the rights of the people. The different governments will control each other, at the same time that each will be controlled by itself. —Federalist No. 51
